The `.cmd` launcher works and is calling the current Python code.

One last comparison batch is running against the reference for the main covered behaviors, then I’ll wrap up with what changed and what was verified.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess, pathlib
nu=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip()
py=['cmd','/c','executable.cmd']
cases=['--version','-c|1 + 2 * 3','-c|[1 2 3] | math sum','-c|1..3','-c|[[a,b]; [1,2] [3,4]] | to json -r','-c|[[lang, gems, grade]; [nu, 100, a]] | reject gems | to json -r',\"-c|('{ \\\"name\\\": \\\"Fred\\\" }' | from json).name\",'-c|open REFERENCE_BINARY.txt | lines | length','-c|char nl','-c|pwd']
failed=0
for item in cases:
    if '|' in item:
        a,b=item.split('|',1); args=[a,b]
    else:
        args=[item]
    r=subprocess.run([nu]+args,capture_output=True)
    p=subprocess.run(py+args,capture_output=True)
    if (r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)"'!=(p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr):
        failed+=1
        print('"'MISMATCH',args)
        print('REF',r.returncode,r.stdout[:200],r.stderr[:100])
        print('PY ',p.returncode,p.stdout[:200],p.stderr[:100])
print('failed',failed)
'@ | python -"

commands.receipt:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
rm -f executable executable.exe executable.cmd executable.bat executable.js executable.jar
cp nushell_port.py executable.py
if [[ "${OS:-}" == "Windows_NT" ]]; then
  cat > executable.cmd <<'EOF'
@echo off
python "%~dp0executable.py" %*
EOF
else
  cp nushell_port.py executable
  chmod +x executable
fi
